You are reading a local Kanban board to help produce a phased build plan for "Kodely", an AI website builder.

Fetch the board:
  curl -s "http://localhost:3001/api/board?boardId=720aa8c1-d259-4e49-b777-c58965efabd1"

It returns JSON: {columns:[{id,name,position}], cards:[{id,columnId,title,description,...}]}.

Read EVERY card (title AND full description) in these columns ONLY:
  - "Pricing & Monetization"
  - "GTM, Marketing & SEO"
  - "Design & UX"
  - "Market & Users"

Write a node script to filter and print them; do not try to read the whole board by eye.

Return a digest with:
1. For each card: a one-line essence in your own words.
2. Classify each as: DECISION (needs a human choice, not engineering), BUILD (real implementation work), or CONTENT (writing/marketing output).
3. For DECISION cards, state precisely what must be decided and what it unblocks.
4. Estimate BUILD cards as S (<1 day), M (2-5 days), L (1-3 weeks), XL (>1 month).
5. Note anything that CONTRADICTS the current product. Facts about the product today: pricing is credit-based (1 credit = $0.002 of model spend, 750 free credits on signup, packs at $9/500, $40/2500, $90/6000); Stripe is fully wired but inert until real keys are set; there are NO subscription tiers; generated sites are FRONTEND-ONLY (no database, auth or payments in generated output); hosting is a *.kodely.site subdomain, no custom domains yet.

Be concise per card. Flag contradictions clearly — several cards were written before a product pivot and describe things that are not true. Return the digest as your final message; it is data for me, not a human-facing report.

10	--- [Market & Users #1] Category has multiple proven $100M+ ARR breakouts ---
11	This is not a speculative niche — it has produced the fastest revenue ramps in software history. Lovable hit **$100M ARR in 8 months**, $200M by Nov 2025, and a $500M run-rate by June 2026 ([Sifted](https://sifted.eu/articles/lovable-hits-100m-arr), [aifundingtracker](https://aifundingtracker.com/lovable-vibe-coding-revenue/)). Demand is real and monetizes fast; the risk is differentiation and retention, not market existence.

Implied free→paid conversion is ~2-3% of registered users, but revenue-per-employee ran ~$6.7M (10-15x SaaS average) because the product is self-serve. Kodely should model a low single-digit paid conversion on a large free top-of-funnel, not high-touch sales.

16	--- [Market & Users #3] Core target segments to prioritize ---
17	Leaders concentrate on: (1) **non-technical founders** building MVPs (no-code lets them ship in 2-6 weeks vs. an $80K-$150K/yr dev hire — [Million Labs](https://millionlabs.co.uk/blog-article/building-your-mvp-a-non-technical-founder-s-guide-to-no-code-development)); (2) **indie hackers** shipping real products; (3) **agencies** reselling client apps; (4) **SMBs** needing internal tools; (5) **designers** turning mockups into working apps; and (6) **developers** who want to skip boilerplate. Kodely retention hinges on closing this last-mile gap (guided prompting, error self-healing, editable output) — it's the single biggest churn lever.

188	
189	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #12] Launch playbook: single-tweet launch + Product Hunt ---
190	Bolt.new **launched with a single tweet on Oct 3, 2024** and became the 2nd-fastest-growing product in history behind ChatGPT ([startupspells](https://startupspells.com/p/bolt-new-second-fastest-growing-product-history-behind-chatgpt)). Product Hunt remains a core launch surface, and Lovable coaches users on driving traffic via 'Lovable Launched, Social, Product Hunt.' Kodely should plan a coordinated launch moment (PH + demo video + creator seeding) rather than a soft rollout — this category rewards a big splashy launch.
191	
192	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #13] Paid ads: geo-arbitrage + heavy creative testing ---
193	Lovable tested LinkedIn ads in Eastern Europe (Romania, Poland, Lithuania) at **40-60% lower CPCs before US scaling**, and ran **100+ simultaneous Facebook/Instagram ad variants**, favoring video over static ([milkandcookies](https://milkandcookies.studio/marketing-spotlight-mapping-lovables-marketing-and-sales-tactics/)). When Kodely turns on paid, test creative volume and cheaper geos first to find winning hooks before scaling to expensive US inventory. Paid is a scale lever, not the primary engine (that's free tier + virality).
194	
195	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #14] Manage reviews/social proof (G2, Trustpilot) deliberately ---
196	Lovable holds a **4.65/5 on G2**, features logos (Google, Amazon, Stripe, Shopify), actively removes fake entries, and keeps transparent negative pricing reviews to build trust vs. suspicious 5.0s ([milkandcookies](https://milkandcookies.studio/marketing-spotlight-mapping-lovables-marketing-and-sales-tactics/)). Comparison sites (SourceForge, AlternativeTo, JoinSecret) are high-intent discovery surfaces. Kodely should actively cultivate G2/Trustpilot presence and claim listings on comparison directories early.
197	
198	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #15] Per-category prompt guides as SEO content ---
199	Publish 'How to prompt Kodely for a [SaaS app / booking site / store / internal tool]' guides — they feed the wizard's templates AND capture high-intent long-tail search (the cheapest SEO wins). Doubles as onboarding content and comparison-page fuel; reuse Nxeon's existing SEO content engine.
200	
201	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #16] Template gallery as an SEO + social-proof surface ---
202	Every public template/remix is an indexable page carrying a 'Built with Kodely' badge — a discovery/SEO surface AND a viral distribution node (Lovable's badge drove ~25K signups/mo). Curate for quality; each template links to its category prompt guide.
203	
204	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #17] Co-brand the go-live moment: 'Hosting by Nxeon, a Kodely partner' ---
205	Present Nxeon as a NAMED hosting partner (logo + 'a Kodely partner') at the go-live step, not a hidden backend. Reinforces the two-isolated-systems model, gives Nxeon its own brand exposure to Kodely's audience, and reads as a trusted recommendation rather than an upsell. The partnership framing is reusable — 'Hosting by Nxeon' can power other builders/front-ends later.
206	
207	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #18] Positioning line: 'Claude writes code. Kodely gives you a live business.' ---
208	Adopt a clear anti-'thin-wrapper' positioning across the homepage, comparison pages and ads. Kodely's promise is a running, hosted, owned business asset — not code you then have to assemble, secure and deploy. Reinforce with the go-live-with-Nxeon bundle and 'you own the code' proof. Pairs with the 'Kodely vs [raw AI / dev tools]' SEO comparison set.
209	
210	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #19] Waitlist + invite waves ---
211	A waitlist with staged invites to control load at launch and manufacture demand. Reuse Nxeon patterns.
212	
213	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #20] Launch plan: ProductHunt / HN / founder video / Discord ---
214	A concrete launch sequence — ProductHunt + Hacker News + founder-led short-form demo video + a Discord community. Category CAC is high; earned/community channels win.
215	
216	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #21] Docs, help center, changelog & public roadmap ---
217	Product docs, a searchable help center, a changelog, and a public roadmap. Supports onboarding, SEO long-tail, and trust.
218	
219	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #22] Activation metric + North Star + funnel instrumentation ---
220	Define the North Star ('first successful DEPLOYED build') and instrument the activation funnel. The board knows every competitor's tactic but never defines how Kodely MEASURES and drives activation→conversion→expansion.
221	
222	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #23] Lifecycle / onboarding email sequence ---
223	Welcome → first-build nudge → credit-wall trigger → go-live-with-Nxeon → win-back. Entirely absent; the cheapest activation+conversion lever. Reuse Nxeon Mail.
224	
225	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #24] PLG loop instrumentation ---
226	Measure badge→signup, remix→signup, and referral attribution so the viral loops are optimizable, not just asserted.
227	
228	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #25] KOL / agency lifetime-commission partner program ---
229	A defined-economics partner program (distinct from the generic affiliate card) mirroring the Nxeon referral model — the cheapest high-ACV channel for a \$500-800-CAC category, dovetailing with Nxeon hosting resale.
230	
231	--- [GTM, Marketing & SEO #26] Positioning / messaging house ---
232	A full message hierarchy + competitive narrative beyond the single line 'Claude writes code. Kodely gives you a live business.' — the source of truth for site, ads, and comparison pages.
233	
234	
235	########## COLUMN: Design & UX  (14 cards) ##########
236	
237	--- [Design & UX #1] First-run prompt box as the entire homepage ---
238	The category-defining first-run pattern (rocket.new, Lovable, Bolt, v0) is a single large centered prompt textarea on the landing page — no signup wall before the first generation. Kodely's home should be one hero prompt with example chips ('CRM for a gym', 'SaaS pricing page') and a subtle model/stack selector. Defer auth until the user wants to save/deploy so the first magic moment happens in seconds. Refs: https://www.rocket.new/ai-app-builder , https://lovable.dev/
239	
240	--- [Design & UX #2] Diff view with approve / reject before applying ---
241	Show a green-additions/red-deletions diff (inline in chat and per-file) of what the agent proposes before it lands, with per-hunk accept/reject and an 'auto-approve' toggle for power users, then a post-run review + rollback of unwanted hunks. This is how users trust the agent and catch when it 'changed the wrong thing'. Refs: https://devops.com/gemini-code-assist-gets-agent-auto-approve-inline-diffs-and-custom-commands-to-speed-up-the-core-coding-loop/ , https://github.com/christianalfoni/agent-diff-view
242	
243	--- [Design & UX #3] Chat/plan mode vs Agent/build mode separation ---
244	Lovable splits an interactive Chat Mode (plan, debug, reason — no code changes) from Agent Mode (executes the build). A read-only planning mode is also a critical safety rail: Replit added a 'planning/chat-only mode' to enforce code freezes after its agent destroyed a production DB. Kodely should let users think/plan without mutating the project. Refs: https://docs.lovable.dev/ , https://blog.replit.com/doubling-down-on-our-commitment-to-secure-vibe-coding
245	
246	--- [Design & UX #4] Make the builder UI itself usable on mobile/tablet ---
247	The builders themselves are desktop-first; the three-pane chat+code+preview layout collapses badly on small screens. Kodely should ship a mobile builder mode (stacked/tabbed chat ↔ preview, hide the code pane, larger touch targets) so users can prompt and preview from a phone — a genuine gap in the market. Ref: https://designrevision.com/blog/forge-vs-bolt-vs-lovable-vs-v0-comparison
248	
249	--- [Design & UX #5] Project dashboard: list, rename, duplicate, deploy status ---
250	A home dashboard listing all projects with thumbnails, last-edited, deploy/domain status, and quick actions (open, duplicate, delete, export to GitHub). Rocket.new/Bolt organize work per-project with export and one-click deploy; make deploy state (draft / published / custom domain) visible at a glance. Refs: https://www.rocket.new/ai-app-builder , https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new
251	
252	--- [Design & UX #6] Template gallery + community remix ---
253	Offer a starter template gallery (SaaS dashboard, landing page, marketplace, portal, storefront) and a 'remix this' flow so users fork an existing public project as a starting point. v0 leans on shadcn/Tailwind primitives; a curated, on-brand template set reduces the cold-start problem and showcases quality. Refs: https://www.bitcot.com/top-10-ui-components-you-can-create-with-v0-by-vercel/ , https://websiteprompts.ai/
254	
255	--- [Design & UX #7] Guided onboarding + prompt-quality coaching ---
256	First-time users write weak prompts and get weak results; whole cottage industries sell 'prompts for Lovable/Bolt'. Bake in an onboarding that suggests structure (goal, pages, style, data), offers example prompts, and can auto-expand a terse prompt into a fuller spec before building. This directly improves first-generation success and retention. Ref: https://www.idlen.io/blog/10-best-prompts-lovable-bolt-cursor/
257	
258	--- [Design & UX #8] Design-import: Figma / screenshot → app ---
259	Rocket.new and v0 both import Figma files (and images) and convert them into live, editable layouts, removing manual design-to-code translation. A screenshot-to-UI path ('clone this look') is a strong acquisition hook. Consider this a fast-follow once core generation is solid. Refs: https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction , https://vercel.com/blog/announcing-v0-generative-ui
260	
261	--- [Design & UX #9] Precision edits via slash-commands ---
262	Rocket.new's 'Precision Mode' exposes 100+ slash commands for targeted edits (e.g. add a route, wire an API, add auth) — deterministic shortcuts that avoid vague prompting and reduce token spend on common operations. A curated slash-command palette is a good power-user layer over the chat. Ref: https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction
263	
264	--- [Design & UX #10] Three-tier prompt help: chips + wizard + auto-enhance ---
265	Attack the #1 beginner churn driver ('I didn't know what to describe') with help at three altitudes, all optional: (1) example chips + template gallery for speed, (2) a base-prompt WIZARD for the unsure, (3) auto-enhance for free-form typers. The raw prompt box stays the default hero; help is opt-in, never a gate. Improving first-build success is the strongest determinant of retention.
266	
267	--- [Design & UX #11] Base-prompt wizard: category → questions → editable spec ---
268	3-4 skippable steps: (1) What are you building? (business site / SaaS / internal tool / store / booking / portfolio / directory / dashboard) — deterministically selects stack, template & guardrails; (2) a few tuned questions per type (needs login? payments? key pages?); (3) look & feel (theme / logo / colors / tone); (4) review the composed spec + estimated credit cost, edit, then Build. Produces an EDITABLE prompt (transparency) and doubles as the plan-before-you-spend step.
269	
270	--- [Design & UX #12] Brand/style step to kill the generic 'AI purple' ---
271	The wizard's look-and-feel step (pick a distinctive theme, upload logo + brand colors, set tone) attacks the well-documented 'every AI app looks the same violet' weakness and feeds design tokens into the system prompt so output stays on-brand. Kodely's demoable design-quality differentiator, surfaced at the very first step.
272	
273	--- [Design & UX #13] Auto-enhance: expand a rough prompt into a full spec ---
274	For users who just type 'a website for my bakery,' a cheap/fast model expands it into a structured spec (pages, features, data, style) BEFORE building — shown to the user to tweak, never done invisibly. Zero friction, big first-result quality jump. rocket.new and others ship a version of this.
275	
276	--- [Design & UX #14] Never force the wizard — raw box stays the default ---
277	Power users hate gates; the hero stays a single big prompt box. The wizard is an obvious 'Not sure where to start? Guide me' path beside it. Keep it fast (3-4 quick, skippable questions) so speed-to-first-build is never sacrificed to a long survey.

# CROSS-CUTTING CONTRADICTIONS (flagged)

1. **The Nxeon hosting funnel doesn't exist.** P14, P17, P18, P26, P27, G17, G23, G25, M12, and partly M9/P13 all assume: a paid Nxeon hosting subscription, custom domains, first-month-free hosting promo, always-on vs sleeping free sites, backups, Nxeon Mail, and a "bring it online" conversion moment. Today: hosting is a free *.kodely.site subdomain, no custom domains. This is ~10 cards of pre-pivot strategy resting on a product that isn't there. **The single biggest reconciliation item on the board** — it's also where most of the monetization thinking lives, so killing it leaves a monetization gap.
2. **Subscription tiers don't exist.** P7, P10, P12, P16 ("per-plan ceilings"), P20 ("plan selection"), P23, P24, P26, G2 ("removable on paid") assume monthly plans with included credit allowances. Product is pure one-off credit packs. P23 is explicitly recorded as a *decision* for the hybrid model — it is now contradicted by shipped behavior and must be either re-affirmed (and built) or formally reversed.
3. **Credit-unit incompatibility.** Every competitor benchmark on this board treats a credit as ~$0.25 of value (Rocket: 100 credits = $25). A Kodely credit is $0.002 of model spend — ~125x smaller. Cards P2, P5, P6, P7, P15, G1 compare raw credit *counts* across systems; all of that math is meaningless as written. Kodely's "750 free credits" reads generous but is ~$1.50 of inference; "500 credits for $9" reads stingy next to "100 credits for $25". This is a live *marketing* hazard, not just a research nit — P25 ("what 1 credit buys") is the fix and should be treated as blocking any published pricing page.
4. **Frontend-only vs "production-ready" positioning.** M7, M8, M10, G18 ("a live business"), D9 ("add auth", "wire an API"), D11 ("needs login? payments?") all assume or promise backend, auth, payments, or production-grade full-stack output. Generated sites have none. Any comparison page (G8) or messaging house (G26) built on these cards will make claims the product cannot honor.
5. **Agency / white-label wedge has no product surface.** M9, P13, G5, G25 — needs client workspaces, white-label branding, seats, and custom domains. None exist; it is at minimum XL, and gated behind items 1 and 2 above.
6. **Duplicates to merge before planning:** template gallery (G3 = G16 = D6); badge+referral (P22 = G2); launch plan (G12 = G20); affiliate vs KOL program (G4 vs G25).
7. **Self-flagged staleness:** M14 carries a `RECONCILE 2026-08-17` note saying its own TAM/ARR figures are outdated and that two TAM figures on the board use different market definitions.

**Compatible-today shortlist** (no contradiction, real leverage): P21 spend caps, P25 credit mapping + estimator, P16 cost telemetry/model routing, P15 credit-wall instrumentation, G22 North Star + funnel, D13 auto-enhance, D12 brand/style step, D2 diff view, D1 hero prompt box.
